refnamediv.refpurpose: Summary statistics for matrices, tables or timeseries

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis:
summary(X) summary(X, dim) summary(X, dim, statistics) S = summary(X [, dim, statistics])
summary(t) summary(t, statistics) summary(t, statistics, datavars) S = summary(t, statistics, datavars)

listitem.para: matrix of doubles, integers, booleans, strings, durations or datetimes.
dimension along which statistics are computed.
string (optional). Specifies which statistics to compute. Possible values are:
"default" (default value): computes a standard set of statistics (NumMissing, Min, Median, Max, Mean, Std)
Statistics may also be a string vector containing individual statistics names.
string (optional). Only for tables and timeseries. Names of variables to include in the summary. Default is "all", meaning all variables are summarized.
A structure containing the summary information for each variable.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: summary() provides a concise overview of the contents of an array, table or timeseries. Depending on the data type, it reports descriptive statistics, metadata and missing value information. summary is intended as a quick exploratory tool for inspecting data before further analysis.
For numeric, datetime and duration data, summary computes descriptive statistics such as minimum, maximum, median, mean and standard deviation.
For boolean and string data, summary reports value distributions and occurrence counts.
For tables and timeseries, summary processes each variable independently and also reports variable metadata such as descriptions and units.

If no output argument is specified, the summary is displayed in the console. When an output argument is requested, summary returns a structure. For arrays, statistics are stored at the first level of the returned structure. For tables and timeseries, statistics are stored inside the structure associated with each variable. (see Output Structure section)

refsection.title: Output Structure
refsection.para: When an output argument is provided, summary() returns a structure containing the computed information.
The organization of the returned structure depends on the input data type.
For matrices, each field of the structure corresponds to a computed statistic.
The value stored in each field contains one element per summarized row or column.
For tables and timeseries, the returned structure contains one field per summarized variable.
Each variable field contains metadata and the requested statistics.

refsection.title: Supported Statistics for Numeric Data
refsection.para:
Depending on the selected options, the following statistics may be computed:
NumMissing: number of missing values (%nan or NaT)
Min: minimum value
Max: maximum value
Median: median value
Mean: mean value
Std: standard deviation
Var: variance
Q1: first quartile (25th percentile)
Q3: third quartile (75th percentile)
Mode: mode
Range: range of values
Sum: sum of values
NumUnique: number of unique non-missing values
Nnz: number of non-zero values
Supported numeric-like types include double, integer, duration and datetime values.

refsection.title: Boolean Variables
refsection.para:
For boolean variables, the summary reports:
True: number of true values
False: number of false values

refsection.title: String Variables
refsection.para:
For string variables, the summary reports:
NumMissing: number of undefined values
Values: unique string values
Counts: occurrence count of each value

refsection.title: Missing Values
refsection.para: Missing values (%nan and NaT) are ignored when computing descriptive statistics. Their number is reported by the NumMissing statistic.

para.screen:
--> t = table([1; 2; %nan], [10; 20; 30], ... > "VariableNames", ["A", "B"]);
--> t.Properties.VariableDescriptions = ["First variable", "Second variable"];
--> t.Properties.VariableUnits = ["m", "s"];
// Display default summary
--> summary(t)
table: [3x2 table]
Variables: A: double Description: First variable Units: m B: double Description: Second variable Units: s
Statistics for numeric data: A B _________ ___
NumMissing 1 0 Min 1 10 Median 1 20 Max 2 30 Mean 1.5 20 Std 0.7071068 10
// Summary without statistics
--> summary(t, "none")
table: [3x2 table]
Variables: A: double Description: First variable Units: m B: double Description: Second variable Units: s
// Summary with all statistics
--> summary(t, "allstats")
table: [3x2 table]
Variables: A: double Description: First variable Units: m B: double Description: Second variable Units: s
Statistics for numeric data: A B _________ ___
NumMissing 1 0 Min 1 10 Median 1 20 Max 2 30 Q1 1 10 Mean 1.5 20 Q3 2 30 Std 0.7071068 10 Var 0.5 100 Mode 1 10 Range 1 20 Sum 3 60 NumUnique 2 3 Nnz 2 3
// Summary for selected variables
--> summary(t, "default", "A")
table: [3x2 table]
Variables: A: double Description: First variable Units: m
Statistics for numeric data: A _________
NumMissing 1 Min 1 Median 1 Max 2 Mean 1.5 Std 0.7071068
// Return summary as a structure
--> S = summary(t)
